title: Breaking Down the United Healthcare Disaster: What’s REALLY Going On? | Real Eisman Playbook Ep. 26
summary: Michael Ha explains why UnitedHealth difficulties extend beyond insurance pricing to Optum Health, risk-adjustment changes and the quality of reported earnings. Eisman presses for a plain-language model, adopts concern about coding exposure and criticizes limited granular disclosure.
assessment: The episode identifies real Optum pressure and a disclosed V28 funding headwind. Guest forecasts of a prolonged decline must be separated from Eisman disclosure-based caution. Several causal allegations remain unproved, and the discussion confuses the MLR ceiling on nonmedical spending with a guaranteed profit margin. Subsequent results show partial recovery, not proof that every structural issue has disappeared.
framework_points: Separate the insurance business from care delivery and pharmacy services.
Distinguish repricing a short-duration contract from repairing a structurally impaired business.
Question recurring earnings supported by asset sales.
Require enough segment disclosure to test the investment thesis.
transcript_cautions: Automatic captions repeatedly misspell Optum, Baird and corporate names. Original review prose corrects them.
Opening montage repeats later discussion and is not counted twice.
Allegations about coding, internal charges and sale arrangements are preserved as hypotheses or reports, not established fraud.
2026 segment realignment changes comparability of Optum figures.
speaker_map_notes: Michael Ha supplies the sell-side research and forecasts. Steve Eisman asks questions, sometimes explicitly adopts a premise, and gives his own disclosure-based investment view. These roles remain separate.
